actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Primitives to apply; the action is used at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed for VIMAEnvBase.seed and the task generator (non-negative)
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset_world

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.
actions.name: seed_world

facts.text: The public factory is vima_bench.make, which returns a VIMAEnvBase
VIMAEnvBase is a gym.Env subclass
The README calls the interface Gym-style and shows make(task_name=...), env.reset()
VIMA-Bench is a PyBullet simulation of a UR5 workspace: reset loads the plane, workspace and UR5 URDFs and sets gravity to -9.8 m/s^2
The constructor defaults are hz=240 and max_sim_steps_to_static=1000
VIMAEnvBase sets p.setTimeStep(1.0 / hz), the physics integration step
One VIMAEnvBase.step with an action executes one pick-and-place primitive and then steps the simulation until the rigid bodies are static, for at most max_sim_steps_to_static steps
The action space is a Dict of four Boxes: pose0_position and pose1_position are [0.25, -0.5] to [0.75, 0.50], and pose0_rotation and pose1_rotation are -1.0 to 1.0 with four elements
step reads the four action keys pose0_position, pose0_rotation, pose1_position and pose1_rotation
step returns the legacy four-tuple (obs, reward, done, info)
The reward is always 0 in VIMA-Bench
done is the task's success or failure flag
The info dict carries the prompt, success and failure
The default observation modalities are rgb and segm, each a Dict over the camera views, plus an ee Discrete(2) indicator
A task's default observation image size is (128, 256) and its default views are front and top
The observations are rendered per view; ee is 0 for the Suction end effector and 1 for Spatula
reset reloads the scene, resets the task, generates the prompt and returns the first observation
reset generates the prompt with Task.generate_prompt, which returns the prompt string and an assets dict
seed creates a numpy default_rng, stores the seed and seeds the task generator
Task.set_seed creates the task's numpy default_rng and stores the seed
Some task code draws from Python's global random and numpy's global generator, which VIMAEnvBase.seed does not set
close disconnects the PyBullet client
The install requirements are pybullet and gym==0.21.0

determinism.notes: reset(seed) and cap.world.seed.v1 call VIMAEnvBase.seed, which makes a numpy default_rng and seeds the task generator (base.py:224-229, task_suite/base.py:141-143); not every upstream draw is controlled by that seed (a gap below). The package fake uses Python's random.Random instead, so one seed does not give the same trajectory on the fake and upstream

gaps: one cap.world.step.v1 tick is one VIMAEnvBase.step primitive, not one physics step: the primitive moves the arm and then integrates until the rigid bodies are static (at most max_sim_steps_to_static = 1000 steps, base.py:36-37 and :425-433), so the simulated duration of one tick is not fixed; timestep_ms names the PyBullet physics step (1/hz, hz default 240)

the package fake is a pure Python kinematic stand-in: it moves one placeholder object to the place position and never uses PyBullet, contact dynamics, the UR5, the assets or the task success/failure logic; its object, target and prompt are placeholders

the fake observation arrays are 3 x 2 x 2 rgb and 2 x 2 segm placeholders for the front and top views; the real arrays are 3 x 128 x 256 and 128 x 256 by the task defaults (task_suite/base.py:67), so the fake returns much smaller arrays than the device

the fake draws with Python's random.Random, upstream with numpy's default_rng; the fake was never compared with the upstream PyBullet environment (pybullet and gym are not installed where the gate runs) and the model was never validated against a physical robot

the upstream path is not fully reproducible from the seed alone: some task code also draws from Python's global random (tasks/task_suite/base.py:560) and numpy's global generator (tasks/task_suite/base.py:599), which VIMAEnvBase.seed does not set; the fake is reproducible from its own seed but does not model those draws
no wall-clock pacing (realtime_factor 0); the fake does not model the physics step or the settle loop
rendering is not served: the clone renders rgb/segm/depth through render_camera and cap.world.render.v1 needs an artifact store; depth is also rejected by the clone's modality assertion (base.py:67)
snapshot and restore are not offered: VIMAEnvBase exposes no get_state/set_state
prompt_assets (the images the prompt refers to) is not exposed; the prompt string is readable through the info read after a reset or a step

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step, reset or seed is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the stored observation, tick and prompt stay readable
